title: Telemetry resilience and pager triage playbook (experiment log)
content:
Summary:
This is a working playbook and experiment log capturing a set of lightweight mitigations we ran in November 2025 to reduce pager churn from transient telemetry failures and noisy SLO burns. Goal: reduce actionable pagers from false-positive signal sources by 40% while preserving time-to-detect for true customer-impacting incidents.

Why this doc exists (background):
- Over the last quarter on-call rotations, we observed a pattern: short-lived metric gaps + synthetic-check flaps led to high-priority PagerDuty alerts that required O(10min) triage each.
- Root causes were heterogeneous: exporter restarts, Prometheus scrape backlog, dashboards with tight anomaly thresholds, and a small proportion were genuine service issues.
- Previous tactics (global quiet windows, blanket suppression) reduce noise but also delay detection. This doc captures experimental rules and runbook edits that aim for surgical suppression and clearer ownership.

Observed symptoms (examples from recent incidents):
- metric:request_count dropped to 0 for 2–6 minutes for a subset of instances while CPU and logs showed normal activity.
- synthetic heartbeat alerts firing repeatedly during control-plane maintenance.
- SLO-burn alert (error-rate-derived) spiking to critical level for < 10 minutes and recovering without user reports.

Hypotheses:
1) Many short alerts are caused by telemetry supply-chain gaps (exporter crash, scrape timeout) rather than user-impacting errors.
2) Suppression windows tuned to the service's scrapes and CPU schedules can eliminate a lot of noise without increasing mean time to detection (MTTD) for real failures.
3) Adding a lightweight impact-score that correlates metric drops with user-facing signals (errors, 5xx, latency, support tickets) will let PD escalate only when correlation suggests real impact.

Experiment plan (staged):
- Stage 0 (observation): add labels to existing alerts indicating scraped_target and scrape_latency. Tag historical pager events with these labels for retrospective analysis. (Done: PD-2982)
- Stage 1 (soft suppression): for alerts that are strictly "single-metric drops" with no correlated 5xx or user-facing latency change, add a 3-minute auto-mute that posts to #sre-telemetry instead of Paging. If the same alert recurs twice within 10 minutes, escalate to paging.
- Stage 2 (source-based debounce): introduce a source-level debounce for exporters with >75% scrape-failure rate across targets for 5m; only page if error budget impact is observed.
- Stage 3 (impact-score routing): compute a simple score = weighted(5xx_count, user_lat_p99_delta, support_ticket_count, metric_drop_duration). If score < threshold, log and notify; if >= threshold, page.

Quick runbook edits (on-call triage flow):
1) When you receive a telemetry-related page, first check: is there an active maintenance window (Slack #infra-ops)?
2) Run quick signal correlation (promql snippets below) and check synthetic heartbeat panel in Grafana.
3) If the metric drop is isolated to exporter label or a single AZ and there is no user-facing latency increase, mark as "telemetry-supply" and follow the temporary muting procedure: add 3m mute, post context to #sre-telemetry, create PD follow-up ticket if recurring.
4) If multiple independent signals correlate (errors up, latency up, support spike), treat as "infrastructure-impact" and follow standard incident runbook.

PromQL and queries we used (examples):
- scrape fail rate by job: sum(rate(prometheus_scrape_sample_scraped[5m]) == 0) by (job)  // simplified; adapt to our metric names
- exporter availability: sum(up{job=~"exporter-.*"} == 0) by (instance)
- correlated error spike: increase(http_server_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])
- combined quick check (pseudo):
  (increase(http_server_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]) > 10) OR (increase(support_incoming_count[15m]) > 2)

Experiment results (early observations):
- Soft suppression (3min auto-mute) reduced pager volume labelled "telemetry-supply" by ~48% over two weeks on the Canary cohort (backend-api svc).
- Median MTTD for true-impact incidents did not materially change in the canary group (within noise).
- Two false negatives: we missed a short-lived cache node failure that only surfaced via telemetry and no immediate 5xx spike; we adjusted the impact-score to weight cache-miss-derived metrics higher.

Operational checklist for adopting changes cluster-wide:
- Add exporter/scrape labels to all telemetry-based PagerDuty alert payloads (automation ticket: GH-frontend/4567).
- Create a new Grafana panel "telemetry supply chain" showing per-job scrape success, exporter restarts, and scrape duration percentiles.
- Implement the 3m soft suppression in Alertmanager for rules tagged with annotation:telemetry_supply = "true" and limit to team-owned services first.
- Add a scheduled job to rehydrate historical pager events with scrape labels for 90 days to validate recall.

Runbook edits (concrete text to add):
- New definition: "telemetry-supply" alert = single metric drop that meets X/Y pattern (one metric, <10min, exporter_present).
- Pager rule: telemetry-supply alerts go to PD webhook with severity=low; initial action is to post to #sre-telemetry and runcorrelate; escalation flow if repeat within 10m or correlated user-impact.

Dashboards and dashboards queries to create/update:
- "Telemetry Supply Overview" (by job/instance): scrape success rate, exporter restarts, scrape duration p95, last successful sample timestamp.
- "Impact Correlator" (for each alert): shows side-by-side panels of request 5xx, p99 latency, synthetic-check success rate, and support ticket rate.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How to tune the 3-minute suppression without missing very short real incidents? We saw one miss; can we make suppression conditional on exporter restart counts?
- Ownership clarity: which team is responsible for exporter reliability vs. metric rule sensitivity? Proposal: rule authorship remains with the team that owns the metric; SRE owns suppression patterns and global tooling.
- Compliance with on-call SLAs: does soft suppression violate the SRE SLA policy for paging on severe SLO burn? We need legal/product signoff for any changes that change escalation timing for SLO-generated alerts.

Next steps and owners:
- Implement labels on alert payloads (owner: Mateo) — target: 2025-12-15
- Deploy 3m soft suppression to canary services (owner: Priya) — target: 2025-12-01
- Build Grafana "Telemetry Supply Overview" dashboard (owner: Owen) — target: 2025-12-08
- Postmortem template update to include "telemetry-supply" classification (owner: Leah) — target: 2025-12-10

Notes-to-self / loose ideas to try later:
- Consider a short-lived adaptive threshold that increases anomaly thresholds during known noisy maintenance windows that are not customer-impacting.
- Machine-learned classifier over 30-day history to predict whether an event is supply vs. impact — but keep rule-based path for predictability.
- Add a lightweight evidence-collector with links to logs and recent exporter pods to the Alert body to speed triage.

References and related artifacts:
- Confluence: telemetry-resilience page (link in metadata)
- PD ticket history: PD-2982
- GH: automation and alert changes: GH-frontend/4567

If you are on-call and this doc conflicts with playbook text in Confluence, follow Confluence for incident escalation and use this as the experiment log. Add any experiment outcomes as comments here so we can fold them into the authoritative playbook.

-- end of log entry for 2025-11 experiment series --
